questions.question: Describe the concept of the color triangle in relation to cone excitation.
questions.solution_html:
• The color triangle represents color perception based on the three cone types in the
  • retina — red (L), green (M), and blue (S). Any visible color can be represented as
  • a combination of the three cone excitations forming a triangular chromaticity
  • diagram.
  • 2 marks for explaining the three cones and the triangle concept.
  • Validation of Pure Tone Thresholds (Speech Recognition Threshold - SRT)

questions.question: Explain why scotopic (night) vision images appear bluish-green.
questions.solution_html:

  • 507 nm (blue-green region); hence night vision appears bluish-green.
  • 2 marks for reason linked to rods and wavelength.

questions.question: Explain the parts of a transducer.
questions.solution_html:
• Transducers consist of two basic parts which are
  • o The Sensor part senses a particular type of energy. It gives a response according
  • to the physical phenomenon that it senses. The response serves as the input for the
  • transducing element.
  • o The Transducing part converts the energy sensed by the sensor into some other
  • form of energy.

questions.question: Define an endoscope and mention its basic function.
questions.solution_html:
• An Endoscope is a medical tool used to examine organs. It consists of a soft long
  • tube with a small light source and camera at one end which can transmit images to
  • a display.
  • Its basic function is to allow a doctor to look inside the body without major surgery
  • by inserting it through a natural opening, such as the mouth or anus. The camera
  • projects images onto a screen, enabling the physician to diagnose
  • 1 mark for definition, 1 mark for function.

  • It is used to diagnose neurol ogical conditions like epilepsy, slee p disorders, and
  • brain injuries.

questions.question: What is the principle of CT imaging?
questions.solution_html:
• Computed Tomography (CT) Scan is a non-invasive medical imaging procedure that
  • utilizes a combination of X -rays and sophisticated computer technology to create
  • detailed cross-sectional images
  • The fundamental principle of a CT scan relies on the differential attenuation
  • (absorption or scattering) of X-ray beams as they pass through different types of tissue
  • in the body.
  • 1 mark each for describing CT and principle.

questions.question: Explain the function of the interferometer in OCT.
questions.solution_html:
• Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) is a non-invasive, non -contact imaging
  • technique that uses low-coherence near-infrared light and interferometry to obtain
  • high-resolution, cross-sectional images of biological tissues, particularly the retina
  • and optic nerve in ophthalmology.
  • Splitting the light: The interferometer (usually a Michelson interferometer) splits
  • this light into two beams: Sample arm → directed into the ti ssue (eye), Reference
  • arm → directed onto a mirror with a known position
  • Collecting reflections : Light reflects back from different layers of the tissue
  • (retina, cornea, etc.) with varying intensities. At the same time, the reference mirror
  • reflects light back along the reference arm.
  • Producing interference :The interferometer recombines the sample beam and
  • reference beam. Because the light source is low-coherence, interference occurs only
  • when the path length of the sample reflection matches the reference arm within the
  • coherence length. This interference encodes depth information
  • Generating A -scan:By analyzing the interference signal, the OCT system
  • produces an axial reflectivity profile (A -scan) of the tissue. Multiple A -scans
  • arranged side by side give a B-scan (cross-sectional image).
  • 2 mark– OCT definition, 3 mark– role of interference in OCT
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: – OCT definition, – role of interference in OCT

questions.question: Explain the mechanism of light dispersion with the help of a prism
questions.solution_html:
• Dispersion: separation of white light into constituent colors due to variation of
  • refractive index with wavelength.
  • Prism refracts each wavelength at different angles; shorter wavelengths (violet)
  • bend more than longer (red).
  • Formula: n=[sin(A+D)/2]/sin(A/2)
  • Results in spectrum (VIBGYOR).

questions.question: · Describe briefly the process of attenuation of absorption.
questions.solution_html:
• When an ultrasound wave propagates through soft tissue, the energy associated
  • with the wave is gradually lost so that its intensity reduces with distance travelled
  • an effect known as attenuation
  • Caused by absorption, scattering, and reflection.
  • The most important mechanism is absorption, in which ultrasound energy is
  • converted into heat.
  • At low frequencies, the particles are able to move in step with the passing pressure
  • wave and energy associate d with the motion of the particles is effectively passed
  • back to the wave as it moves on.
  • Absorption has been found to be strongly dependent on tissue composition and
  • structure.
  • Tissues with high collagen content such as tendons and cartilage show high
  • absorption, whereas those with high water content show lower absorption.
  • =Water and liquids such as urine, amniotic fluid and blood have low absorption and
  • low attenuation.
  • 1 mark– Attenuation definition, 2 marks – atteneuation of absorption, 2 marks
  • Examples

questions.question: What are the properties of X-rays that make them useful in medical imaging?
questions.solution_html:
• High energy, short wavelength (0.01–10 nm).
  • Penetrate soft tissues but absorbed by dense materials (bone).
  • Cause ionization and fluorescence.
  • Travel in straight lines.
  • Can be recorded on film/detectors to produce contrast images.
  • Any five properties (1 mark each)

questions.question: Why are op-amps widely used in biomedical instruments?
questions.solution_html:
• High input impedance and low output impedance → minimal loading on sensors.
  • High gain → amplify weak physiological signals (e.g., ECG, EEG).
  • =Stable and low noise.
  • Can be configured as filters, amplifiers, integrators, or differentiators.
  • Compact, reliable, and inexpensive.
  • Applications (Ellaborate any three biomedical applications)
  • 2 marks– Op amp properties, 3marks– Biomedical applications

questions.question: Describe the functioning of electromagnetic tracking systems in freehand ultrasound.
questions.solution_html:
• ultrasound.
  • Small transmit device placed near the patient generates a magnetic field.
  • A sensor coil is attached to the ultrasound transducer, and is connected to a
  • receiver.
  • Movement of the coil through the magnetic field induces voltage in the coil from
  • which the receiver estimates the position and orientation in space.
  • These systems do not require line of sight (i.e. a clear uninterrupted path between
  • coil and receiver); however, they may suffer distortions due to the presence of
  • other hospital equipment
  • 2 marks– Components, 2 marks– Working, 1 mark– Application
